statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) across every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 78 (high).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour of this window and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress stays in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September catalyst stack. No danger window is defined.
headline: Full weekend halt window after Friday's two-sided close: hawkish Jackson Hole keynote, Chicago PMI 47.1, NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), VIX 14.43, new Venezuela oil agreement
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August. Pre-halt evidence re-verified this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range. Friday delivered a two-sided macro shock. Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote was read as hawkish, with reporting placing the 2-year yield up about 11 basis points near 4.32 to 4.34 percent, the 10-year near 4.72 percent, and September rate-hike odds re-rated from roughly 35 percent to about 57 to 60 percent; Warsh cited 12-month PCE inflation at 3.7 percent with over half the basket rising faster than 3 percent. Official H.15 readings for 27 August, the latest published, are 2Y 4.20 percent and 10Y 4.67 percent. Against that, the August Chicago PMI collapsed to 47.1 from 57.6 versus consensus near 57.9, a drop of roughly 10.5 points into contraction, and the preliminary nonfarm payrolls annual revision printed -79K. That combination is stagflationary in shape and is treated here as a Stress and Confidence input, not as evidence of the persistent one-way index path Tail measures. Internals into the halt were dispersed rather than aligned: the Dow finished roughly flat, the S&P 500 fell 0.25 percent to 7,711.76 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.52 percent, as hyperscalers advanced and chipmakers retreated, with Nvidia about 3 to 4.5 percent lower after its post-earnings gain the prior session. Dispersion of that kind argues against the aligned structure a higher Tail would require. New verified weekend information since the prior run: President Trump announced an agreement with Venezuela covering 17 fields with a stated 65 billion barrels of proven potential and a 55 percent effective output share for the United States. On the energy side WTI sits near 83.44 dollars and Brent near 88.29 after an approximately 4 percent weekly decline, with the Iran standoff currently read as a sanctions rather than a physical-supply confrontation despite the continuing Strait of Hormuz disruption. Iranian statements this weekend restate that position without new escalation. The shared cross-asset context file was last collected at 02:28 UTC, well outside its 90-minute freshness window, so it is excluded as current structure evidence and this assessment rests entirely on independently verified sources. No pathological price path can form while the venue is closed, so Tail is held at 5 across all 24 slots, the dominant mode is normal in every hour, the mapped policy state stays EA_ON and no danger window is defined. Stress runs 25 to 29 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates, and Confidence eases from 78 to 72 purely as Friday's prints age. The next evidence checkpoint is the Globex reopen on Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, beyond this window, followed by the 1 to 4 September catalyst stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP and the Beige Book, jobless claims, trade balance and ISM Services, and August payrolls.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover Friday's cash session and the first ten hours of the weekend halt. Tail ran 11 to 13 with Stress in the low-to-mid 50s through the Asian and European hours as positioning built ahead of the Jackson Hole keynote. The mode shifted to event/whipsaw from 14:00 UTC as the Chicago PMI miss and then the keynote hit the tape, and Tail peaked at 22 with Stress at 64 in the 16:00 to 19:00 UTC block; the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH because retracements kept occurring. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the readings decayed quickly, Tail from 12 to 5 and Stress from 52 to 25, as the venue entered its weekend closure and the mode reverted to normal. One hour, 10:00 UTC on 28 August, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form; Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify. Stress runs 25 to 29 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates, carrying the unresolved September policy question, Friday's Chicago PMI contraction and negative payroll revision, the newly announced Venezuela oil agreement, and the 1 to 4 September catalyst stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP and the Beige Book, jobless claims and trade balance, ISM Services, and August payrolls. Confidence eases from 78 to 72 purely as Friday's verified prints age; coverage of levels, yields, volatility, oil, geopolitics and the calendar is complete but cannot be refreshed until the venue reopens. The Globex reopen on Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC lies beyond the final slot, so reopening structure is explicitly not forecast here.
